cards.text: Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, have teamed up against Jerusalem, and the hearts of King Ahaz of Judah and his people tremble like trees in the wind (Isaiah 7:1-2). Now the prophet Isaiah tells us what the LORD says to him next. Take a large scroll, the LORD says, and write on it with an ordinary stylus: Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

cards.question: The LORD wants this scroll on the record, so He will appoint ___ witnesses for it.

cards.text: The LORD picks the two: Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah. Then the prophetess conceives and gives birth to a son, and Isaiah's a dad again.

cards.question: Isaiah's new son is born. What does the LORD tell Isaiah to name him?

cards.text: Five letters on my handle, friend, and this boy needs the LARGE scroll. Then the LORD sets a clock: before the boy knows how to cry ‘Father’ or ‘Mother,’ something is going to happen to Damascus and Samaria.

cards.question: Before Isaiah's son knows how to cry ‘Father’ or ‘Mother,’ the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off.
Who carries off the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria?

cards.text: And the LORD's still talking: this people has rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah. Friend, gently flowing water is the sound people play on their phones to fall asleep, and they said NO THANKS.

cards.question: This people rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah. Who did they rejoice in instead?

answers.text: Rezin and the son of Remaliah
Ahaz and the house of David

cards.question: Because this people rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah, what will the Lord bring against them?

answers.text: The mighty floodwaters of the Euphrates
A quiet stream from the Jordan
A long dry season with no rain

cards.question: In the LORD's picture, the mighty floodwaters of the Euphrates stand for the king of Assyria and all his pomp.

cards.text: They passed on the gentle water, so here comes the FIRE HOSE. It overflows its channels and overruns its banks.

cards.question: The flood of the Euphrates overflows its banks and pours into ___.

cards.text: It swirls and sweeps over Judah, reaching all the way up to the neck. Up to the NECK, friend: you're still breathing, but you are NOT having a good day.
The LORD says its spreading streams will cover “your entire land, O Immanuel!” That's the name from the sign the Lord gave Ahaz: a son called Immanuel (Isaiah 7:14).
Then the LORD calls out to the peoples and all the distant lands: huddle together, pay attention, prepare for battle. And “prepare for battle” comes up TWICE.

cards.question: The peoples huddle together and prepare for battle. What does the LORD say will happen to them?
After calling the peoples to prepare for battle, the LORD says, “Devise a plan.” True or false: He says their plan will happen.
Every plan the peoples devise will be thwarted, and every proposal will not happen. What reason does the LORD give?

answers.text: For their kings are too weak

cards.text: Remember that name from the flood, Immanuel? Matthew tells us it means “God with us” (Matthew 1:23), and that's the very thought the LORD ends this message on.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 18 quotes "Devise a plan.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 20 quotes "God with us", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Card 1 says the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz is written on the scroll. Card 4 then asks what the son is named, with that same name as the right answer, so the baker only has to match a word already shown.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "The LORD wants this scroll on the record" ties the witnesses to the scroll and gives a reason for them. Isaiah 8:2 doesn't say what the witnesses are for or how they connect to the scroll.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Isaiah's a dad again" depends on an earlier son (Shear-jashub, Isaiah 7:3), which is a fact from outside the passage, but the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: "Five letters on my handle" is a callback to the name carved on his handle, which is never set up in this lesson. The joke also says the boy needs the large scroll, but the scroll was written in 8:1, before the boy was born. That blends the joke with the Bible setting and suggests a reason for the scroll's size that the text never gives. A stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: "The sign the Lord gave Ahaz" names Ahaz as the one receiving the sign. Isaiah 7:13-14 gives it to "you" after "Hear now, O house of David," so who receives the sign should stay as the text has it.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Every plan the peoples devise will be thwarted, and every proposal will not happen" stretches Isaiah 8:10, which says "Devise a plan, but it will be thwarted; state a proposal, but it will not happen."

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
